1.5. MALARIA IN PREGNANCY

Tertian Malaria – 48 hours’ cycle – P ovale, vivax, falciparum

Quartan Malaria – 72 hours’ cycle – P Malariae.

Immunity lost within 2 years.

Gold std Test: microscopic examination of thick & thin film.

Incidences:

75% falciparum, 0.5 – 1% Mortality

5.5% ovale 12.9% vivax, 2.1% Malariae

Suspect malaria:

Fever + history of travel to endemic area or residence (> 6m0).

Recent return 3 weeks – viral infections.

Chemoprophylaxis not 100% effective.

 

 

S/S + investigations – Rapid Testing + blood film (1 hour).

Other Tests – CBC, BSL, U/E, blood C/S, urine dip, stool, CXR, USG.

Blood film shows:

No evidence of Malaria.

Falciparum.

Non-Falciparum.

1. No evidence of Malaria:

Repeat film – (after stopping prophylaxis).

3 negative films 12 – 24 hours.

apart exclude malaria so finish chemoprophylaxis.

Empirical Treatment – Severe malaria expected.

Stop prophylaxis before repeating (as it give negative report).

2. Non – Falciparum:

Chloroquine – 600mg stat dose

300mg – 6 – 8 hours later.

300mg – Day 2.

300mg – Day 3.

To prevent relapse (vivax/ovale).

300mg – weekly chloroquine.

During pregnancy chloroquine resistant cases are treated by mefloquine.

To prevent relapse after delivery and testing for G6PD , primaquine is recommended. (avoid in pregnancy).

3. Falciparum:

Mixed species or not characterized.

Admit.

Assess severity.

Complicated.

Uncomplicated.

Complicated:

Admit in HDU

>2% parasitized

50% mortality.

Antimalarial immediately.

Fluid balance – CVP line.

Monitoring.

BSL – 1 hourly

4 hourly

HR.

Temp

RR.

SPo2.

JVP.

Repeat daily.

CBC

Parasite count.

LFT, RFT, clotting screen.

Treat for G negative bacteria.

Artesunate I/V 2.4mg/kg @ 0, 12, 24hours’ stat dose (drugs of choice any Gestation, then daily till patient is stable).

Quinine I/V 20mg/ kg in 5% D/W over 4 hours. Then 100mg/kg every 8 hours then oral when Pt can swallow.

Uncomplicated:

Admit in ward

<2% parasitemia

Mortality 0.1%

Quinine 600mg 8 hourly + clindamycin 450mg 8 hourly (before 13 weeks drug of choice).

OR

Raiment 4-tab, B.D for 3days.

OR

Proguanil + Atovaquone (malarone) 4 doses daily – 3 days.

Some important points about Malaria:

Expert advice (especially recurrent & severe).

Rapid detection negative in low parasitemia & P – vivax.

Gold std microscopy thin/thick film.

Rapid detection followed by microscopy (Number of infected cells, species, stage).

Premunition: Natural immunity acquired against malaria.

Low premunition – 90% with low premunition develop anemia.

UK population low premonition.

Relapses – due to planta sequestration:

25 – 42 days’ average, relapse time

85 days after quinine.

98 days after Artesunate.

63 days with artemether, lumefantrine

Weekly films – reduces mortality due to recurrence.

treatment of recurrence => artesunate 84% success. Artesunate 100mg/ day for 7 days + clindamycin 45mg TDS – 7 days (WHO recommendation for relapse).

Hypoglycemia exacerbation by quinine => fetal distress.

Cinchonism, 7 days’ treatment:

Headache.

Nausea.

Diarrhea.

Vomiting.

Blurred vision.

Auditory problems.

Hypoglycemia – due to hyper insulinemia.

commonest S/E of quinine.

Infection control specialist => recurrent/ severe cases.

Treatment of complications:

Pulmonary edema – JVP aim of rt arterial pressure <10cm H2O, (it has 50% mortality)

Anemia Hb <8:

Pack cell + I/V frusemide 20mg.

Exchange transfusion.

Secondary bacterial infection when pt become hypotensive systolic B.P <80mg

C/S => start ceftriaxone immediately due to risk of infection.

 

Thrombocytopenia:

Recovers 7 days in 90%.

& 100% within 14 days

Of treatment.

Thrombocytopenia is risk

Of blood loss in endemic

Areas but not PPH.

Fetal complications:

IUGR, Pre – Term, fetal distress.

MDT – severe fetal compromise.

(ICU specialist, infectious disease specialist, obstetrician, neonatologist).

Aim is to prevent pre – term, IUD.

VTE Prophylaxis:

Plt <100, - withhold.

Peripartum Malaria:

Placental sequestration => P Falciparum most common:

Is indication for following tests:

placental histopathology

Cord & baby blood film To detect

Every week for 28 weeks.

Congenital malaria 8-33%

 

Positive

Inform women regarding S/S of malaria in Baby.

=> All Neonates of mother who had malaria in pregnancy had blood films @ birth & weekly blood films for 28 days.

 

 

Care of women after recovery from Malaria:

Regular ANC, HB, Glucose, Growth scan, Plt.

FGR – 50% - Routine IUGR care.

Pre term labour => tocolysis + steroid + antimalarial.

Fetal distress => Antipyretics (PCM 1g every 4 – hours – max 4g/day) BSL monitoring

Still birth + pre – Term birth prevented by effective antimalarial treatment.

Miscarriages

IUD – Antimalarial can prevent IUD.

Complicated Malaria:

1 of following:

Impaired consciousness.

Hypoglycemia < 2.2 mmol.

ARDS, pulmonary edema.

Parasitemia > 2%.

Severe anemia < 8.

DIC.

Hemoglobinuria without GOPD deficiency.

Renal impairment:

Oliguria, 0.4ml/hr.

Creatinine > 265 mmol.

Hyper lacticaemia:

Correlated with mortality.

Shock.

Acidosis < 7.3.

Algal malaria – gm negative septicemia.

Jaundice is not a complicated feature.

Malaria prevention ABCD

Awareness of risk.

Bite prevention.

Chemo prophylaxis.

Diagnose + treat promptly.

 

Awareness of risk:

Avoid traveling to endemic areas.

Guidance on avoidance.

Specific risk associated with travel.

Educate on symptoms.

 

Bite prevention:

Repellents – 50% Deet.

Knock – down sprays.

Insecticide treated nets repeat every 6m0.

Clothing.

Room protection.

 

Chemo prophylaxis

not 100% not effective.

Casual prophylaxis

Continue for 7 days after leaving.

Against liver schizont.

Malarone (atovaquone + proguanil).

1 tab daily.

Avoid in 1st

Suppressive:

Continue for 4 weeks after leaving.

Red blood cell stage.

Mefloquine 1 tablet/ week.

Drug of choice in 2nd and 3rd

Other drugs for chemoprophylaxis:

Proguanil + chloroquine.

Not effective in chloroquine resistant areas

Doxycycline + primaquine:

CI in pregnancy.

Primaquine:

Cause Hemolysis in G6PD.

C/I in G6PD deficiency.

Mefloquine:

Safe in 1st and B.F.

Chloroquine

Safe in pregnancy but resistance.

Mefloquine given in chloroquine resistance.

Diagnose and Treat promptly:

Quinine 600mg TDS – 7 days.

Clindamycin 450mg TDS 5 – 7 days.

Vomiting within ½ hours – repeat full dose.

Vomiting within 30 – 60 min – repeat ½ dose.

Treatment finished then mefloquine is given after 1 week of last dose.

Coartem & atovaquone & proguanil can be used if not given in prophylaxis.
